title: Per-tenant graceful throttle manager with multi-region failover and model-aware trip logic
creator: Marco Nguyen
description: Design and implement a per-tenant graceful throttle manager that computes and enforces circuit/trip decisions using a combination of SLO-aware signals (error-rate, p95 latency, queue depth), model-specific risk profiles, and regional capacity heuristics. When a tenant or dependency trips, the system should execute safe fallbacks in a deterministic, observable, and reversible way: model variant fallback, token-budget reduction, cached-response surfaces, and progressive shedding of non-essential features. This ticket covers the runtime control-plane + controller, policy DSL, metrics, tests, and a staged rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria:
- Per-tenant policy object can be persisted and read by the runtime controller (policy versioning + TTL)
- Trip decision uses weighted composite score of error-rate, p95 latency, and queue depth with configurable hysteresis windows
- Safe fallback actions implemented: (1) route to compatible model variant, (2) apply token-budget cap, (3) return cached prefix when available, (4) degrade optional tool/function calls
- Multi-region priorities respected: controller routes to secondary region with no more than 15% extra latency on failover tests
- Admin override and emergency-open API present and audited
- Dashboards show per-tenant trip state, cause breakdown, and rollback controls
- End-to-end chaos test that simulates dependency latency spike leads to controlled shedding, not complete outage
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
1) Policy DSL: small JSON schema representing trip thresholds (error_rate_pct, p95_ms, queue_depth), weights, hysteresis (window_sec, cooloff_sec), and ordered fallback actions. Policies live in config-store (consul/etcd) with version hashes.
2) Scoring: compute normalized signals over sliding windows (default 60s) -> weighted sum -> compare to threshold with separate trip and recovery thresholds to provide hysteresis.
3) Model-aware modifiers: each model/dependency has a risk score; for high-risk models (large-context, long-tail failure modes) multiply score to bias earlier trips. Tenant-level priority and business tier adjust thresholds (enterprise tenants have wider tolerance but smaller token-shedding aggressiveness).
4) Fallback choreography: controller emits an ordered plan (action sequence). Runtime executes actions atomically where possible: start with cheap actions (token_budget, reduce_sampling) -> route to smaller quantized variant -> fall back to cached prefix or low-cost reranker -> finally soft-deny with user-friendly message or queued retry. Each step records reason and metrics.
5) Multi-region: controller has region-aware topology + real-time latency map. On trip, controller computes candidate regions with compatible model variants and capacity headroom. Prefer active-active routing; only failover when local score exceeds region local_threshold or headroom < min_capacity.
6) Observability: emit trip_event, action_exec, recovery_event with tags {tenant, model, dependency, region, policy_version, cause}. Build dashboard and alert rules.
7) Safety: safety gate for automated fallback must not apply to tenants with explicit locked_policies (admin lock). Emergency open API (audit-logged) to force isolation.
8) Persistence & replay: policy changes are versioned; controller persists last-known state for each tenant to allow graceful restart without unsafe replays.

Notes on trade-offs:
- We choose weighted composite scoring instead of single-metric breakers to better correlate SLO violations across bursty workloads. This increases complexity of tuning but reduces noisy false trips.
- Model-aware modifiers add operational maintenance (risk profiles must be kept up to date) but allow earlier protection for brittle models.

Implementation tasks (tentative):
- runtime controller API and state machine (ENG runtime team)
- policy schema + admin UI to edit policies (Console UX follow-up)
- persistence layer integration (etcd)
- executor hooks in serving runtime (safe action API)
- telemetry + dashboards (Observability)
- chaos test and perf bench (SRE)
telemetry_metrics:
List of metrics we will emit (for dashboards/alerting):
- redwood.circuit.trip_count{tenant,model,region,cause} (counter)
- redwood.circuit.current_state{tenant,model,region} (gauge: 0=closed,1=half-open,2=open)
- redwood.circuit.score{tenant,model,region} (gauge: composite score)
- redwood.latency.p95{tenant,model,region} (histogram)
- redwood.error_rate.1m{tenant,dependency} (gauge)
- redwood.queue_depth{service,region} (gauge)
- redwood.fallback.action_exec_count{tenant,action} (counter)
- redwood.fallback.recovery_time{tenant} (histogram)
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation (edge cases on hysteresis, weight scaling)
- Integration test: inject synthetic high-latency into dependency service and assert fallback sequence executed in order
- Multi-region failover test: run replayed traffic in staging with primary region blackholed; verify progressive failover and SLA on tail latency
- Load test at scale across 1k tenants with mixed model profiles to validate controller throughput and config-store load
- Chaos experiment: random partial failures + slow joins, ensure no cascading opens across unrelated tenants
- Postmortem runbook creation after initial rollout
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging): enable per-tenant policy evaluation in dry-run mode for 2 weeks, collect metrics and false-positive rate.
Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 10 low-risk tenants with automated action throttling set to 'warn' for first 48 hrs, then 'enforce' if stable.
Phase 3 (tiered rollout): expand to enterprise tier tenants with higher thresholds, then to all tenants over 4 weeks.
Phase 4 (global): enable multi-region automatic failover for tenants opted-in.
Rollback strategy: metadata allows instant disable of automated actions per-tenant; global fail-safe is a cluster-wide 'no-automated-fallback' flag that switches controller to detect-only mode.
